title: GCS-02: Unauthorized GCS Detected in Device List

lines.msg: New device entry: GCS-04 (MAC: 915-0A-1F-3C-7D-4E). No record of GCS-04 in fleet register. MAC not in inventory.
RTK-1: GNSS fix lost. Satellite count: 12 → 0. Sky clear. No weather event.
UAS-11: Aircraft GNSS fix lost. Position jumped 150m north. No known motion or wind event.
915 MHz link quality: 94% → 12% in 0.4 seconds. No known interference source.
UAS-11: RTK-1 and aircraft GNSS both lost fix simultaneously under clear sky.
UAS-11: DAA-1 telemetry shows position as 43.1724°N, 77.5631°W. GCS-02 shows 43.1719°N, 77.5635°W.
UAS-11: Home point updated to 43.1721°N, 77.5633°W. No command received from RPIC.
UAS-11: Flight controller received command to set home point. No RPIC input logged.
UAS-11: Command injection detected. Firmware hash matches baseline.
UAS-11: DAA-1 and GCS-02 disagree on aircraft position. Discrepancy: 0.0005° (approx. 55m).
UAS-11: No user input received from RPIC at 09:15:30.
Log export initiated by HUOG-OPS-03. All logs preserved to HUOG-NAS01: /incidents/20261022/GCS-02-091802

instructorNote: This inject confirms the presence of a rogue GCS. The technical team must immediately isolate GCS-02 and preserve all logs. Watch for attempts to reboot or re-pair the 915 MHz link.

citations.headingPath: ISP › Section 9 › 9.1 C2 link compromise, interference or GNSS spoofing
citations.quote: Indicators: commands the RPIC did not send; a second controller or ground station in the device list; telemetry that disagrees with what the VO sees; GNSS position jumps, satellite count drop under cl

citations.documentTitle: Harwick UAS Operations Group — UAS Flight Operations & Safety Manual (FOM)
citations.headingPath: FOM › Section 9 › 9.3 GNSS degradation or spoofing suspicion
citations.quote: Signs: satellite count falls while the sky is clear; position jumps; RTK fix lost on both RTK-1 and the aircraft; the home point moves; DAA-1 and the GCS disagree on position. Actions: the RPIC switch
